title: Indices, Reports, International Institutions & Key Concepts

blocks.text: Financial and Development Indices
Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index)
Published by: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
Frequency: Annual (released in July)
Purpose: Measures progress across three parameters:
Access (35%), Usage (45%), and Quality (20%).
Score Range: 0 = Complete financial exclusion; 100 = Full financial inclusion.
Fiscal Health Index (FHI)
Published by: NITI Aayog.
Purpose: Evaluates fiscal health of Indian states and promote transparency in state finances.
Data Source: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
Key Indicators: Quality of expenditure, revenue mobilization, fiscal prudence, debt index, fiscal sustainability.
Gender inequality index elt is Published by UNDP eIt measures gender disparities across three dimensions: reproductive health, empowerment, and labour market participation.
Lesser the value of GII= Better the performance.
Multidimensional Vulnerability Index (MVI)
Launched by: United Nations General Assembly.
Year: August 2024
Purpose: Measures structural vulnerability and lack of resilience in developing countries, especially Small Island Developing States.
Purpose: Evaluates innovation ecosystem of Indian states and Union Territories and promotes competitive federalism.
Environmental Performance Index (EPI)
Published by: Yale University and Columbia University.
Partner: World Economic Forum (WEF)
Purpose: Measures environmental health and ecosystem vitality and tracks progress toward Sustainable Development Goals.
Corruption Perception Index (CPI)
Published by: Transparency International.
Scale: 0 = Highly corrupt; 100 = Very clean.
Ranks countries based on perceived public sector corruption.
World Competitiveness Index
Published by: International Institute for Management Development (IMD)
Measures global economic competitiveness.
World Press Freedom Index
Published by: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
Measures the level of press freedom worldwide.
School Education Quality Index (SEQI)
First released: September 2019.
Evaluates state performance in school education.
Export Preparedness Index (EPI)
Launched: August 2020.
Ranks Indian states based on export readiness.

International Economic Institutions and Agreements World Trade Organization (WTO)
A global organization that regulates international trade and promotes rules - based trade among nations.
General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)
Signed in 1947.
Reduced tariffs and trade barriers
Replaced by WTO in 1995
General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS)
Extends global trade rules to services
Four modes: cross-border supply, consumption abroad, commercial presence, movement of natural persons.
Agreement on Agriculture (AoA)
Effective from 1995 (WTO Agreement)
Objective: Reduce trade-distorting agricultural subsidies Types of Subsidies:

Major Government Initiatives
Startup India launched in 2016 under DPIIT.
Mission Antyodaya adopted in Union Budget 2017-18. ePAT scheme launched in 2012 by Bureau of Energy Efficiency.
Make in India launched September 25, 2014.
POSHAN Abhiyaan launched March 8, 2018.
Service Exports from India Scheme operated 2015-2020.
Infrastructure Initiatives
National Infrastructure Pipeline launched in 2020. eSagarmala Programme launched in 2015.
Bharatmala Pariyojana launched in 2017.
National Technical Textiles Mission launched in 2020 by Ministry of Textiles.
Budget: 21480 crore till 2025-26.
Financial Platforms eTrade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) helps MSMEs discount invoices and access quick liquidity.

Financial and Regulatory Institutions eIndustrial Finance Corporation of India established July 1, 1948. eClearing Corporation of India Limited established April 2001. eTelecom Regulatory Authority of India established February 20, 1997.
National Stock Exchange established 1992; operations began 1994.
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority established 2003.

Investment and Real Estate Regulation eForeign Investment Promotion Board established 1991 and abolished May 24, 2017. eFDI approvals now processed through Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal under DPIIT.

A long-term contract between government and _ private sector to deliver public assets or services while sharing risks.
Examples include Eastern Peripheral Expressway, Delhi- Meerut Expressway and Chenani-Nashri Tunnel.
Greenfield: new infrastructure built on unused land
Brownfield: upgrading or renovating existing infrastructure ECONOMIC COMMITTEES
